title: A Horizon for the Provision
premise: Desert ranger Sebastian Thornbury has chased the thief Wren across the salt flats for months, both of them running from pasts that punish stillness. When a flash flood uncovers a chest bearing the seal of Karavel, a nation erased from maps twenty years ago, Sebastian and Wren are forced into an uneasy alliance to decide its fate: sell it, return it, or use it to resurrect a claim that could get them killed. Sheltering from monsoon season with a river ferryman named Odessa and her leaking boat, they discover the chest holds proof of who betrayed Karavel — and that the betrayer's descendants still rule the coast. In the climax, pursued by hired blades as the dry season opens, they choose justice outside the law, delivering the evidence to Karavel's scattered survivors instead of the courts that failed them. The book ends with Sebastian finally stopping — not because it's safe, but because he's found people worth staying for.
about_author: Jonah Brightwater is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on monsoon waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who find families in the most inhospitable places on earth.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Wouldn't Stop
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. He corners Wren in a canyon after months of pursuit, but a flash flood separates them and unearths a sealed chest stamped with Karavel's dead crest. Wren steals it; Sebastian gives chase into the lowlands. Emotional beat: the hollow compulsion of pursuit — Sebastian realizes he no longer remembers why catching Wren matters.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sebastian and Wren. Both seek shelter from the coming monsoon aboard Odessa's half-sunken ferry; she demands labor in exchange for deck space. Forced proximity cracks their hostility, and together they open the chest: documents naming the men who sold Karavel to its conquerors. Emotional beat: wary trust forming over shared meals and bilge pumps.

chapters.title: Monsoon, and Men With Knives
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. Hired blades arrive at the river settlement hunting the chest, forcing the trio downstream through storm-swollen rapids in the leaking boat. Wren confesses she stole from Karavel's survivors once and owes them; Sebastian admits his ranger badge was revoked for refusing an unjust order. Emotional beat: found family crystallizing under fire.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Provision
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. As the dry season opens, the pursuers corner them at the delta. Instead of selling the chest or surrendering it to corrupt authorities, they fight through to Karavel's refugee enclave and hand the evidence to the survivors themselves. The betrayers' names spread; justice moves without a courtroom. Emotional beat: Sebastian chooses to stay — belonging won over escape.
